item.text: I’m looking for the next refactor that improves cohesion instead of just expanding the API. The main remaining weakness is that heap construction, copying, and bulk-loading are spread across multiple entry points, so I’m targeting a single internal build path and a cleaner set of convenience operations on top of it.

I’m making two concrete improvements: a first-class `replaceMin` operation in the canonical API, and a single internal construction path for the heap core so copying and heapified builds don’t keep reinventing themselves. Then I’ll extend the tests around heap-to-heap transfer and root replacement.
I’m updating the public wrapper and the internal heap engine together so `replaceMin` is efficient at the root and the heap constructors flow through one private array-based build path.

The core change is in, but the constructor refactor needs one Java-specific cleanup: `this(...)` has to be the first statement. I’m fixing that and then I’ll add tests for heap-to-heap bulk transfer and root replacement.

I’m extending the tests now to cover the new canonical operations instead of only indirect behavior. That means one test for `replaceMin` and one for `addAll(IntHeap)` so the interface-level convenience methods are actually validated.
The refactor and test coverage are both updated. I’m compiling with deprecation lint again now to catch any constructor-flow or default-method regressions before I close this pass.

That makes a common heap mutation explicit in the API instead of forcing every caller through `removeMin` plus `offer`.

I also refactored [IntBinaryHeap.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/011_binary_heap/IntBinaryHeap.java:22) so all construction paths flow through one private array-based constructor, with validation/copy helpers factored out.
